newsitem.title: USA: Mourners grieve Mexican executed in Texas.
newsitem.headline: Mourners grieve Mexican executed in Texas.

text.p: About 200 mourners attended a Mass on Thursday for a Mexican man whose execution in Texas sparked protests on both sides of the border.

The Mass was celebrated for Irineo Tristan Montoya one day after he was executed by lethal injection for his role in the 1985 murder of a Texas man stabbed to death near the U.S-Mexico border in Brownsville, Texas.
"We are going, little one," Emilia Montoya said through tears as she leaned over her son's coffin after the Mass at a Houston funeral home attended by an estimated 200 people.

Many of the mourners filing past the open coffin reached down to touch Tristan's body, which was to be flown to Brownsville and then transported to the family's village in the northern Mexican border state of Tamaulipas for burial.
"I am taking my boy down there because he asked me to do that," said Onorio Tristan, who witnessed his son's execution at the Huntsville State Prison, 70 miles (112 km) north of Houston.

Tristan, the second Mexican executed in Texas since capital punishment resumed in 1982, was put to death despite diplomatic protests and a public outcry from Mexico, where there is no capital punishment except in military cases.
His fate was sealed when the U.S. Supreme Court refused to review whether his rights under an international treaty were violated and Texas Gov. George Bush ignored pleas for a last-minute reprieve.
"Bush, assassin, we won't vote for you again," several women shouted in Spanish as they left the funeral home.
Tristan was convicted for the 1985 murder of John Kilheffer, who was stabbed more than 22 times and his body dumped in a grapefruit grove near the Rio Grande.
